comparisons.peer_topic: OTC Derivatives Credit Exposure and Risk Management
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit exposure on OTC derivatives arises primarily from market-making activities to provide client liquidity and manage market risk. The company manages this exposure using established credit risk processes, bilateral collateral arrangements requiring daily exchanges, and Credit Valuation Adjustments (CVA) to reflect counterparty credit risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose the use of Credit Valuation Adjustments (CVA) in their derivatives reporting, linking CVA to counterparty credit risk. JPMorgan presents results net of centrally-managed CVA and other valuation adjustments, primarily in principal transactions revenue. Goldman Sachs explicitly states that CVA is included in the fair value of derivatives to reflect counterparty credit risk, arising from market-making activities. Both firms treat CVA as a central component of managing and presenting derivative fair values and credit exposure.

sentences.text: (b)Consists primarily of centrally-managed credit valuation adjustments ("CVA"), funding valuation adjustments ("FVA") on derivatives, other valuation adjustments, and certain components of fair value option elected liabilities, which are primarily reported in principal transactions revenue.
Results are presented net of associated hedging activities and net of CVA and FVA amounts allocated to Fixed Income Markets and Equity Markets.
Our credit exposure on OTC derivatives arises primarily from our market-making activities.

As credit risk is an essential component of fair value, we include a credit valuation adjustment (CVA) in the fair value of derivatives to reflect counterparty credit risk, as described in Note 7 to the consolidated financial statements.
